messages:
maria: Heads-up — opened a PR that touches request routing + KV cache eviction. Need architecture signoff before we can merge. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8427 RFC: https://internal.redwood.ai/rfcs/221-shard-routing-change

vikram: Thanks — can you call out exactly which guarantees change? is this strictly a routing optimization or are we changing consistency/ordering?

maria: Short list:
- routing policy now prefers cold-cache replicas for tail-latency heavy requests (configurable)
- KV cache eviction becomes async (small window where stale KV might be used)
- fallback to previous model variant on capacity failure retained

olivia: Async eviction is the one I want clarity on. need to know stale window and how it affects SLOs. also any durability concerns for Private deployments?

maria: initial numbers from local perf run:
```
scenario: 1k qps, avg seq=128
baseline: 8.2ms p50 / 48ms p99
w/ async-evict: 8.4ms p50 / 51ms p99
cache-stale-window: ~120-200ms worst case (config: cache.async_evict_ms)
```
these are microbenchmarks — will run canary in staging next. Private deployments: eviction still happens locally, no cross-tenant effect.

alex: I can do a quick check on the canary plan. we should add a rollback/force-sync toggle and an audit event for eviction ops. Can you add a short note in the PR describing rollback and metrics to watch?

maria: yep — adding rollback toggle and a metrics section (cache_hit_ratio, kv_stale_rate, p99_latency). Will update PR in next hour.

ci-bot: build #8427 passed unit & integration tests — no regressions detected. :white_check_mark:

vikram: once you update the PR, @olivia and I will review for arch. tagging arch-oncall (cc @olivia). if we get ACK before Friday EOD we can merge and schedule a small-staged canary over weekend.

maria: filing a tiny RFC appendix with the eviction trade-offs now and linking it in the PR. holding merge until arch ACK. thanks all. :pray:
